messages.subject: lm in RStanARM
parts:
I'm trying to run a simple model using RStanARM, 
> stanlm (kid_score ~ mom_hs, data=kidiq)
but it's giving me this error
Error in model.frame.default(formula = formula, data = data, subset = subset,  : 
  invalid type (closure) for variable '(weights)'
Is this the proper way to call stanlm? [I used the same format as I would for lm since the readme file says you can call stanlm in the same way]


Peter

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: lm in RStanARM
parts:
That is a bug. For the time being, you can just call stanglm with the (default) Gaussian likelihood

stanglm(kid_score ~ mom_hs, data=kidiq)

which is all stanlm() is supposed to be doing anyway.

Ben

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: lm in RStanARM
parts:
I think when K = 2, there are elements below are vector of length 1.  By default, a vector of length 1 in R corresponds to a scalar in Stan.  To fix this, you need to make those data explicitly arrays in R such as 

df <- 2
prior_df <- array(df, dim = c(length(df))

--
Jiqiang

messages.subject: logical -> int in stan()
parts:
Hi Mav,

For glm(), this works

glm(RTEN > 8 ~ INTG + ORAL + WRIT, data = USJudgeRatings, family = binomial())

but not for stanglm()

> stanglm(RTEN > 8 ~ INTG + ORAL + WRIT, data = USJudgeRatings, family = binomial())
Error : variable does not exist; processing stage=data initialization; variable name=y; base type=int
In addition: Warning message:
In FUN(c("N", "K", "X", "y", "family", "link", "has_weights", "weights",  :
  data with name y is not numeric and not used
failed to create the sampler

; sampling not done

although this works

stanglm(as.integer(RTEN > 8) ~ INTG + ORAL + WRIT, data = USJudgeRatings, family = binomial())

I could fix this in stanglm(), but is there a reason why stan() doesn't convert logical vectors to integer vectors?

Ben
